cards.text: Friend, Jesus just gave some hard teaching, and a lot of His disciples walked away (John 6:60, 66). After this, Jesus travels all around Galilee. But there's one region He's staying out of: Judea.

cards.question: Why doesn't Jesus want to travel in Judea?

answers.text: The Jews there were trying to kill Him
Herod had banned Him from the region
A famine had spread across the land

cards.text: But the Jewish Feast of Tabernacles is near. And here come Jesus' brothers with ADVICE, because a holiday is coming and family ALWAYS has advice.

cards.question: With the feast coming, Jesus' brothers tell Him to leave Galilee and go to ___.
Why do Jesus' brothers want Him to go to Judea?

answers.text: So His disciples there can see His works
So He can make peace with the leaders
So He can teach in the synagogues there

cards.text: Their pitch: nobody who wants to be known acts in secret, so "show Yourself to the world." Friend, they sound like a manager who just printed business cards.

cards.question: Then John, the writer of this Gospel, adds a quiet note about Jesus' brothers. True or false: His own brothers believed in Him.

cards.text: Jesus answers His brothers, and He talks about timing. Friend, I'm a baker, so you KNOW I respect a man who talks about timing.

cards.question: True or false: Jesus tells His brothers that His time has already come.
Jesus tells His brothers the world can't hate them, but it hates Him. Why does He say it hates Him?

answers.text: He testifies that its works are evil
He takes its crowds away from it

cards.text: Then Jesus tells them, "Go up to the feast on your own." He says He's not going up to this feast, because His time has not yet come.

cards.question: True or false: After telling His brothers this, Jesus stays behind in Galilee.
Once His brothers have gone up to the feast, Jesus goes up too. How does He go?

answers.text: Riding in on a young donkey

cards.text: So at the feast, the Jews are looking for Him and asking, "Where is He?" Friend, I heard that question every time somebody dug through my junk drawer for the scissors.

cards.question: Many in the crowds at the feast are whispering about Jesus. What are they saying?

answers.text: Some call Him good and others a deceiver
Some call Him a prophet and others a madman
Some call Him the Messiah and others a sinner

cards.question: Even so, no one at the feast would speak publicly about Jesus for fear of the ___.

cards.text: And that's where we'll leave it for now, friend. Keep that oven warm, because this feast is just getting started.

findings.problem: The comparison doesn't click. The brothers are pushing Jesus to go public and show Himself to the world. 'A manager who just printed business cards' is about someone promoting themselves, not someone pushing another person into the spotlight. 'Manager' is also unclear: it could mean a boss at work or a talent manager. A baker would need it explained.

rule.text: 2. The everyday comparison must have the same action. ... 4. It clicks instantly for any adult, with no explaining. 5. If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: John 7:6 contrasts the brothers with Jesus: 'your time is always at hand' but His time has not yet come. Cards 8 and 9 never tell the brothers' half of that contrast, and no later card tells it either. The baker misses the point of Jesus' answer. Card 10 builds on the same contrast, that the world can't hate them but hates Him.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The card calls the writer 'John, the writer of this Gospel.' The Gospel never names its author. John 21:24 points only to 'the disciple' who testifies, so no verse can serve as the reference that outside facts need.
findings.question: Can Papa Dorin name a Bible book's traditional author, like John for this Gospel, when the text doesn't name the author? If so, what reference does he give, or can he say something like 'the writer of this Gospel' without naming him?
